stories.headline: PSD and AUR file joint no-confidence motion against Bolojan government, vote scheduled for May 5
stories.summary: Romania's Social Democratic Party left the governing coalition and allied with the far-right Alliance for the Union of Romanians to file a no-confidence motion against Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan's minority government. The motion, formally submitted on April 28, gathered over 250 signatures and is set for a parliamentary vote on May 5; PNL declared it will no longer enter coalition with PSD regardless of the outcome, while President Nicușor Dan faces pressure over his constitutional role in any post-motion government formation.

stories.headline: SAFE defense program management becomes political battlefield as Bolojan and Ciolacu trade blame
stories.summary: A dispute erupted between Prime Minister Bolojan and former PM Ciolacu over who bears responsibility for the management structure of Romania's €16 billion EU SAFE defense program, with Bolojan claiming the scheme was set under the Ciolacu government and Ciolacu countering that the key ordinance was signed by Bolojan's cabinet. AUR leader Simion separately accused both PSD and PNL of a corrupt €10 billion 'financial heist' in the SAFE contracts, with German firm Rheinmetall set to receive roughly €5 billion.

stories.headline: Romania loses €458.7 million from PNRR Payment Request 3; PSD and current government trade blame
stories.summary: The European Commission issued a final decision cutting €458.7 million from Romania's third PNRR payment request, while also releasing €350.7 million that had been suspended, with current government officials blaming the Ciolacu-era failure to complete reforms on time and former PSD minister Adrian Câciu accusing the current Minister of European Projects Dragoș Pîslaru of concealing his own incompetence.

stories.headline: Romanian leu falls to historic lows against euro amid political crisis; BNR says market will stabilize
stories.summary: The Romanian leu depreciated sharply against the euro during the week of April 28–May 1, reaching a historic low of 5.1417 lei per euro at the BNR official rate on April 30, with the interbank market briefly exceeding 5.20 lei. The National Bank attributed the movement to political uncertainty following PSD's exit from the coalition and the no-confidence motion, and said the situation would calm, while BNR Board member Cristian Popa warned the political crisis risks blocking fiscal consolidation.
